I remember the summer I brought some scones to a planned picnic for friends; they said, "Anything that tastes as good as those scones would be perfect!" One the French bread was the bakery's specialty and one of our most popular items. It was made fresh throughout the day. The bakery sat on the main road and a supermarket at the corner would buy our bread in the afternoon to sell fresh next day at five o'clock, After work, Tom, a delivery boy, and I would toss the unsold loaves back into the oven circa ten o'clock and eave them to crust over. Once, I noticed that Tom closely eyed the loaves as they baked. Occasionally, he would take one out ahead of time to dry the bottom crust on the bare oven rack. When it finished, he would remind customers out the door that the bread was tasty still warm. smiling, he was pleased with his little secret. Tom's secret didn't remain a secret for too long, though; Lulu, a regular customer, took notice. I was intrigued, too. She bought one the next time she heard of the secret, and that day I snuck away and took a bite. After that first bite, I was never able to look at or think of French bread the same way again. Warm French bread is particularly wonderful. I can't explain it, but the combination of warmth, crusty texture and flavor evokes childhood memories and arouses comfort and joy. I now try to make time each week to buy a warm loaf of French bread. Many people haven't thought about the special feeling that a daily occurrence can evoke. We go through life, sleepwalking past the little things that do matter, too tired or too hurried to truly pay attention. It's amazing what we miss.
